transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

I can certainly help you with your Beko dishwasher. Gritty bits on glasses are most often caused by a blocked filter, obstructed spray arms, or simply using a gentle programme that doesn't get hot enough to dissolve food particles. To check the most common causes safely, please switch off and unplug the machine first. Then remove the lower rack and twist out the bottom filter to rinse it under the tap, and also spin each spray arm by hand to ensure they aren't stuck or blocked by debris.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok did the filter, its full of food n grease. gonna rinse it. upper spray arm is a bit stiff when i spin it, lower one is fine

Thanks for checking those parts. Since the filter was clogged and the upper arm is stiff, these are likely the main reasons your dishes aren't coming out clean. Please rinse the filter thoroughly and try to clear any debris from the upper spray arm jets so it spins freely again. Once you've done that, please let me know if the cleaning issue persists. If it does, we'll need to look at other causes like water temperature or detergent.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
cleared a few blocked holes on the upper arm w a cocktail stick, filter rinsed too. ran a normal programme after n its much better. do i need the model number for anything?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. You don't need the model number as your issue appears to be fully resolved by cleaning the filter and spray arm. It's great to hear it's working much better now. To stop this from happening again, try to scrape off large food scraps before loading and clean the filter every few washes. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
